EDI.substrand: Language for expressing and developing ideas

ER.substrand: Engaging with and responding to literature

entries.text: Identify how texts are shaped by the purpose and audience they are made for.
Use interaction skills (listening, turn-taking, asking questions) to share ideas; plan and deliver short presentations.
Use comprehension strategies (predicting, questioning, monitoring, summarising) to build literal and inferred meaning; use text features and images to help meaning.
Plan, draft and publish imaginative, informative and persuasive texts with a clear sequence and topic vocabulary.
Understand how different types of texts are organised (e.g. procedures, recounts) and how headings and layout help readers.

entries.substrand: Language for expressing and developing ideas
entries.text: Use topic-specific vocabulary and understand how images and words work together to create meaning.
Explain how texts reflect the contexts, purposes and audiences they are made for.
Use interaction skills to contribute to and clarify discussions; plan and deliver short spoken and multimodal presentations.
Use comprehension strategies to build literal and inferred meaning, find the main idea and supporting details, and connect ideas across texts.
Plan, draft and publish texts with ideas grouped into paragraphs and suitable vocabulary; re-read and edit for meaning.
Understand that language choices (formal or informal, tone) change depending on who we are communicating with and why.
Understand how texts are organised by purpose, and how paragraphs, headings and navigation features help readers find information.

entries.substrand: Language for expressing and developing ideas
entries.text: Use precise and technical vocabulary; understand how complex sentences link ideas.
Explain how texts present ideas, people and issues differently depending on purpose and audience.
Use interaction skills, including active listening and clear speaking, to develop ideas; deliver presentations that suit purpose and audience.
Use comprehension strategies to build literal and inferred meaning and evaluate ideas; navigate print and digital texts using features such as headings, links and tables.
Plan, create, edit and publish texts that suit purpose and audience, using paragraphs, precise vocabulary and multimodal features.
Understand how to move between formal and informal language to suit context and relationship; use language to express opinions.
Understand how informative and persuasive texts use different structures and features, and how cohesive words link ideas.

entries.substrand: Language for expressing and developing ideas
entries.text: Use noun groups, verbs and adverbials to add precise detail; explore how word choice and images create meaning.

entries.substrand: Engaging with and responding to literature
entries.text: Present a personal response to literary texts, explaining likes and dislikes with reasons.
Identify how authors use language features, including imagery and sound, to create effects.
Create narratives and poems drawing on personal experience, using descriptive language and dialogue.
Examine how texts, including digital texts, present information and viewpoints for different purposes and audiences.
Use interaction skills to present and support opinions and respond to others; deliver logically structured presentations with multimodal elements.
Use comprehension strategies to interpret and analyse information, compare information across texts and evaluate the reliability of sources.
Plan, create, edit and publish texts with a logical structure, supporting evidence and language that suits purpose, audience and form.
Understand how language choices, including evaluative and emotive language, show relationships and express viewpoints.
Understand how text structures and features (tables, captions, sections) are used for different purposes, including in digital texts.

entries.substrand: Language for expressing and developing ideas
entries.text: Use a range of sentence types and vocabulary for clarity and effect; understand how visual elements add meaning.

entries.substrand: Engaging with and responding to literature
entries.text: Compare personal responses to literary texts and explain how texts connect to their own experiences.
Identify and explain how figurative language, imagery and sound devices create meaning and effect.
Create literary texts that experiment with structure, voice and language for effect.
Analyse how representations of people, places, events and ideas reflect the contexts in which texts are created.
Use interaction skills to discuss and present ideas, evaluating features of texts; plan and deliver presentations suited to the audience.
Analyse and evaluate how language, structure and multimodal features shape meaning; analyse implicit and explicit ideas.
Plan, create, edit and publish imaginative, informative and persuasive texts, choosing structure, language and multimodal features for the audience.
Understand how language choices, including modality and evaluative language, are used to persuade, express opinions and build relationships.
Understand how structures and features such as headings, cohesive links and layout support purpose in print, digital and multimodal texts.

entries.substrand: Language for expressing and developing ideas
entries.text: Understand how vocabulary (including technical and figurative language) and sentence structures shape meaning; analyse how images and layout create meaning.

entries.substrand: Engaging with and responding to literature
entries.text: Explain personal responses to literary texts, including how texts connect to their own and others’ experiences and values.
Analyse how language features such as figurative language, rhythm and rhyme shape meaning in literary texts, including poetry and song lyrics.
Create literary texts drawing on personal experience, using language and structure for effect.
Analyse how texts are shaped by context and how they position audiences to accept particular viewpoints.
Use interaction skills to discuss, debate and present viewpoints, varying language and delivery for effect.
Evaluate how texts use language and visual techniques to persuade and position readers; analyse and synthesise information from several sources.
Plan, create, edit and publish texts that develop and justify a point of view using evidence and persuasive techniques.
Understand how to adjust register, tone and modality for an audience, and how language can include or exclude people.
Analyse how text structures and conventions are adapted for purpose and audience, including combining text types.

entries.substrand: Language for expressing and developing ideas
entries.text: Analyse and use language features such as emotive vocabulary, nominalisation and figurative language for effect.

entries.substrand: Engaging with and responding to literature
entries.text: Explain and justify responses to literary texts, considering different viewpoints and values.
Analyse how authors use language, structure and voice to create tone, mood and meaning.
Create literary texts that use voice, point of view and language features to engage an audience.
